sections.title: Your army. At every scale.
sections.intro: Inspect a moving part. Pull back and plan the next move.
sections.how: The modern camera moves from a close view of the original models to a broad battlefield overview. At tactical scale, readable team-colored icons take the place of tiny unit silhouettes.
sections.look: the extractor sitting on the metal deposit, normal-size base at 1×, closer models at 2×, and team icons across the whole map.
sections.capture: Twenty-six fresh engine renders move through the real camera’s zoom range. The slider starts at 1×, reaches 2× detail and pulls back to the camera’s whole-map minimum, 0.078125×. Thirty-nine staged units use settled, activated COB poses. The second solar was moved onto clear ground and a metal extractor occupies the deposit. Unit placements stay fixed; the camera pans at wide scales and fog is omitted. Each stop is native 960 × 640; no image is enlarged to simulate camera zoom.

zoomViewer.alt: Greenhaven outpost at the engine’s original 1× camera scale, with the metal extractor on its deposit.
zoomViewer.caption: Greenhaven · staged 39-unit scene · real camera captures · start at 1×, zoom to 2× or the whole map.

sections.title: More than bigger pixels.
sections.intro: Extra detail in the ground and in the trees above it.
sections.how: The close view synthesizes 64 × 64 terrain tiles from the game’s 32 × 32 artwork, alongside 2× feature sprites. Patch matching uses the installed game’s original patterns; the result is cached locally.
sections.look: the leaves and tree edges as well as the grass. The slider changes both terrain and tree artwork, with the camera held at 2×.
sections.capture: A close Greenhaven view is rendered twice through Modern GPU, using original artwork and then real synthesized terrain and foliage. Both captures share the same camera and committed state. Healthy native leaf sprites are used; authored dead stumps are cleared in this staged display. Native 480 × 320 captures show a smaller area at the same 2× camera. Shadow or missing variants keep the engine’s normal fallback.
sections.caption: Greenhaven close-up · same 2× camera · original / synthesized terrain and trees.
sections.altBefore: Original grass and healthy leaf trees at the same close Greenhaven camera
sections.altAfter: The same Greenhaven grass and trees with real 2× synthesized terrain and foliage

sections.title: The blast reaches the armor.
sections.intro: Colored light, soft glow and a sharper view of the battlefield.
sections.how: Visible effects cast colored light onto nearby surfaces. An emission layer adds a soft halo to bright effects, while the modern path renders unit geometry and terrain at detail scale.
sections.look: the nearby Bulldog’s armor catching the explosion. Tap a whole view or drag the divider across the same instant.
sections.capture: A Jeffy self-destructs beside a Bulldog among healthy Greenhaven trees. Classic CPU and Modern GPU share the same committed tick 132 and 2× camera. Modern uses real 2× synthesized terrain and foliage, with default anti-aliasing, lighting and glow at native strengths. The clearing removes burn successors and authored dead stumps; the surrounding trees remain healthy. Full renderer comparison, native 960 × 640.
sections.caption: Greenhaven · same blast, committed tick and 2× camera · healthy tree sprites.
sections.altBefore: A Jeffy explosion beside a Bulldog in Nanolathe’s Classic CPU renderer
sections.altAfter: The same explosion and Bulldog in the Modern GPU renderer with synthesized terrain, lighting and glow

extraMotion.label: Matched Classic and Modern engine footage of a Jeffy explosion beside a Bulldog
extraMotion.caption: Greenhaven · same staged timeline · 3 seconds at 30 FPS · switch views at the same instant.

sections.title: A world beyond the shore.
sections.intro: Wind moves the water. A fleet leaves more than a wake.
sections.how: Switch the water’s treatments independently and watch them react in real time. The study uses original transport and submarine geometry, textures and Gods of War terrain, with water equations adapted from Nanolathe’s modern renderer.
sections.look: the submarine refracting beneath the surface, foam tracing the shore, and the transport’s crane reflected below its hull. Keep the scene paused to compare treatments, or animate the water.
sections.capture: This live WebGL water study uses frozen, activated transport and submarine poses exported at committed tick 31 from engine 617540c5. Original palette textures, the native terrain view and the engine’s projected shoreline mask are retained. Water field, surface shading, damp shoreline, foam, refraction and reflection ripple/tint/opacity arithmetic are adapted at native strengths. The sampled wind direction and tidal rate remain fixed. WebGL triangle/depth rasterization, texture filtering, and reflected-mesh occlusion differ from the native height-key screen-space resolve. It does not simulate units, COB wakes, shadow passes or gameplay. The native Metal engine recording below includes moving units, real wakes and evolving wind.

motion.label: A transport reflects on Gods of War water alongside a refracted submarine and shoreline foam
motion.caption: Native Metal engine capture · Gods of War · transport + submarine · moving units, COB wakes and real session wind · 6 seconds at 30 FPS.

sections.title: Armor with a little more life.
sections.intro: Turn a unit toward the light and see its surfaces respond.
sections.how: Recognized metal textures receive a broad highlight and directional glints. Painted panels have a softer response. The original colors, panel seams and model geometry remain the foundation.
sections.look: the armor highlights moving as you rotate the unit or orbit its light. Switch the finish off and on at a fixed angle.
sections.capture: The original interactive ARM mobile Annihilator is restored. This frozen model and texture atlas were exported from engine 801c8b2. WebGL adapts the engine’s metal/paint finish and glint arithmetic; rotation, tilt and an optional light orbit are study controls. Its projection, depth testing, anti-aliasing and floor shadow differ from the game renderer. It is a material study, not a playable unit. The disclosure below retains a real Metal engine comparison captured at 279f7af1.

motion.label: The original ARM mobile Annihilator rotates in the native engine to show materials and glints
motion.caption: Comet Catcher · staged turntable · materials and glints off / on.

sections.title: Smoother edges. Moving parts too.
sections.intro: Keep diagonals, turrets and small silhouettes readable.
sections.how: Modern anti-aliasing renders model subjects at twice the resolution in each direction. Four coverage samples resolve into each output pixel, blending mobile units and their live pieces into the scene beneath them.
sections.look: the diagonal armor, gun barrels and small silhouettes across nine original models.
sections.capture: Bulldog, Maverick, Zeus, Reaper, Annihilator, Stumpy, Merl, Goliath and a construction Kbot share committed poses and the 2× camera. Both renderer paths have anti-aliasing enabled: Classic retains structure coverage, while Modern extends it to mobile units. Vegetation is cleared from the tableau so it does not hide the models. Whole renderer paths, native 960 × 640.
sections.caption: Matched model lineup · the same camera and poses · whole Classic / Modern rendering paths.
sections.altBefore: An original model lineup showing mobile units and a building in Nanolathe’s Classic CPU renderer
sections.altAfter: The same original models and camera with full-unit anti-aliasing in Nanolathe’s Modern GPU renderer

sections.title: Heat you can see.
sections.intro: The fire stays familiar. The air above it changes.
sections.how: Burning vegetation bends the scene behind a rising heat plume. The original flame and smoke artwork remains visible with the treatment off.
sections.look: grass wavering above the three burning palms; pause and switch shimmer off and on.
sections.capture: Three original architree01 palms are placed and ignited through the real feature service. Session.Step advances their flames, smoke and burning lifecycle. Matched Modern GPU views toggle only FireShimmer. The 2× camera and native effect strength remain fixed; no image resampling or retiming is used.

motion.label: Heat you can see.
motion.caption: Great Divide · staged session · same timeline · 5 seconds at 30 FPS · native 480 × 320 close-up.

sections.title: A blast. A wreck. A slow cool.
sections.intro: What survives the explosion keeps the heat.
sections.how: Fresh wrecks glow and distort the air as they cool, then settle back to their original textures. The death, corpse selection and cooling age all come from the engine.
sections.look: the Stumpy’s wreck warming the scene after the blast, then returning to its normal finish as the heat fades.
sections.capture: A Stumpy takes ordinary nonlethal damage during warmup, then an ordinary lethal damage packet one second into the clip. Its COB Killed result places the real corpse at tick 120. Paired Modern views toggle WreckGlow and WreckShimmer, preserving the explosion, materials and every other effect. The 13-second clip includes cooling and shimmer expiry; native 480 × 320 at the 2× camera.

motion.label: A blast. A wreck. A slow cool.
motion.caption: Great Divide · staged session · same timeline · 13 seconds at 30 FPS · native 480 × 320 close-up.

sections.title: Higher flight. Softer shadows.
sections.intro: A sharp silhouette close to the ground. A softer trace from above.
sections.how: Aircraft shadows spread as height above the receiving surface increases. The modern renderer filters the original silhouette at the native shadow strength, keeping narrow wings connected. Switch the treatment off to see the ordinary shadow.
sections.look: the left plane’s tighter shadow and the right plane’s softer one. Drag across the ground beneath them, or tap a whole view.
sections.capture: Two original CORE Hurricane bombers are staged at 60 and 180 world units above Greenhaven’s ground. Their original activated COB poses, heights, heading and 2× camera stay fixed. The actual Metal renderer executes the same cloned drawlist with only SoftShadows off and on; ShadowSoftness remains 100%. The on/off/on replay restores identical pixels, and the committed publication remains unchanged. Vegetation is omitted from this presentation fixture to keep both shadows visible. This is a frozen altitude study, not simulated flight. Native 960 × 640; no resampling or retouching.
sections.caption: Greenhaven · same planes, heights and camera · lower flight left / higher flight right · native strength.
sections.altBefore: Two CORE Hurricane bombers at different heights with ordinary silhouette shadows on Greenhaven
sections.altAfter: The same two bombers and camera with the modern altitude-dependent soft aircraft shadows

overview.title: Closer views. Wider plans.
overview.text: Free camera zoom from the whole map to 2× detail, with tactical team icons at wide scales.

overview.title: Remastered map art.
overview.text: Local 2× synthesis for terrain and feature sprites, using the original artwork and a reusable cache.

overview.title: Every model, clearer.
overview.text: Anti-aliasing covers mobile units and their animated parts. Presentation interpolation smooths movement between committed ticks.

overview.title: Light across the battlefield.
overview.text: Explosions, fire, projectiles, construction spray and hot wrecks light nearby models, smoke and ground.

overview.title: Glow and impact.
overview.text: Soft emission halos, refractive blast rings and separate glow strengths for weapons, explosions and construction.

overview.title: Water with depth.
overview.text: Wind-driven surface shading and motion, seabed displacement, submerged-hull refraction, coastal foam and rippled reflections.

overview.title: Materials that respond.
overview.text: Metal glints, cooler broad metal highlights and softer painted-panel finishes retain the original colors and seams.

overview.title: Heat that fades.
overview.text: Burning trees shimmer. Fresh wrecks emit warm light and distort the air, then cool naturally.

overview.title: Marks and shadows.
overview.text: Footprints, tank tracks and fading scorch marks remain on the terrain. Aircraft shadows soften with altitude.

overview.title: Classic stays available.
overview.text: Switch between Modern GPU and Classic CPU with F10, or choose in Options → Nanolathe. Display effects are independent of gameplay rules.
